prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (within 500 words)

Economy, tax, and regulation
- Cut £12bn a year in waste by 2007–08 via a civil service hiring freeze, removing 235,000 bureaucratic posts, and abolishing/cutting 168 public bodies.
- Maintain or exceed existing spending on NHS, schools, transport, and international development; increase spending on police, defence, and pensions; overall spending growth at 4% per year (vs. 5% baseline).
- Use £8bn of savings to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts in the first Budget.
- Halve council tax bills for many pensioner households (up to £500, centrally funded); raise the basic state pension in line with earnings; retain Winter Fuel Payment and other benefits.
- Promote saving through a Lifetime Savings Account; strengthen workplace pensions (opt-out default; use unclaimed financial assets to protect failed scheme members).
- Keep Bank of England independence; do not join the euro.
- Reduce regulatory burdens with departmental regulatory budgets, cost-benefit tests, sunset reviews; end “gold-plating” of EU directives; seek restoration of certain EU labour-law opt-outs.

Childcare, schools, and universities
- Flexible maternity pay (higher for 6 months or standard over 9 months).
- Up to £50/week per under-5 for eligible working families’ childcare, with simpler administration and support for informal care; expand workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Additional £15bn a year for schools by 2009–10; discipline reforms giving heads control over admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; reduced teacher paperwork.
- Funding to follow the pupil; publish exam marks alongside grades; allow international qualifications; slimmed National Curriculum; focus on rigour.
- 300,000 vocational grants of £1,000 for 14–16-year-olds; two hours of after-school sport; ban junk food in schools.
- Create 600,000 extra school places; permit growth of popular schools; allow places at independent schools within state cost.
- Moratorium on special school closures; FE reform with “Super college” status; scrap university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; build university endowments.

Healthcare and social care
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn a year in the first Parliament; abolish Strategic Health Authorities; reduce PCTs and quangos; end central hospital targets.
- Greater hospital autonomy; funding follows the patient; protect viable community hospitals; reinstate matrons with powers on cleanliness; strengthen infection control.
- Expand patient and GP choice; partial public contribution for self-funded operations to cut waits.
- Social care partnership so homes need not be sold to pay for long-term care; more respite for carers.
- Improve access to NHS dentistry with payment reform and monthly cover plans.
- Health checks for non-EU entrants staying over 12 months or settling; national STI awareness campaign.

Crime, policing, and security
- Recruit 5,000 extra police annually; cut paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners; focus on visible neighbourhood policing.
- End early release; add 20,000 prison places; “honesty in sentencing.”
- Expand drug treatment, including 25,000 residential places; reverse cannabis reclassification.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; strengthen counterterror measures.

Immigration and asylum
- 24-hour port surveillance; restore embarkation controls; create a unified Border Control Police.
- Points-based work permits prioritising needed skills.
- Annual overall immigration limit including an asylum quota; process asylum outside the UK; take a fixed UNHCR-refugee share; seek updated international/asylum arrangements and national control.

Governance and devolution
- Abolish regional assemblies; return powers (planning, housing, transport, fire) to local authorities.
- Strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; seek a substantially elected second chamber.
- Ensure “English votes for English laws”; maintain commitments to devolution in Scotland, Wales (with a referendum on options), and accountable direct rule in Northern Ireland if needed.

Communities, transport, environment, housing, farming
- More local say in planning; stronger action on illegal traveller encampments; devolve arts and lottery decisions.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Protect green belts; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost energy efficiency, renewables, and recycling.
- Honest food labelling; support local food; require public procurement to meet high UK standards; pursue CAP and fisheries reform; update animal welfare; free vote on hunting with dogs.

Defence, foreign policy, and aid
- Increase frontline defence by £2.7bn by 2007–08; support service families; retain regiments; improve procurement; keep NATO central.
- Commit to Iraq reconstruction; support a Middle East peace based on mutual security and state viability.
- Oppose the EU Constitution (referendum) and euro entry; seek EU reform and further enlargement; greater national control over aid; meet 0.7% ODA by 2013.

Early actions
- Within the first day/month: begin police recruitment; reinstate matrons; first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower head teachers on expulsions; implement 24-hour port surveillance; set a referendum date on the EU Constitution.
